n: Asa’s son Jehoshaphat became king and strengthened Judah’s defenses against Israel.

f.g: Name means ‘the LORD judges’ — fitting for his later reform of the courts.

n: He stationed troops in Judah’s fortified cities and in the Ephraimite towns Asa had captured.
The Lord was with Jehoshaphat because he followed the early example of David and did not seek the Baals.

f.w: the first ways of his father David
f.g: David’s earlier, faithful years (some manuscripts lack ‘David,’ pointing to Asa’s early ways).
Plural of Baal — the Canaanite storm and fertility gods.

n: He sought the God of his fathers and obeyed His commands, not the practices of the northern kingdom.

f.g: The calf worship and Baal worship of the northern kingdom.

n: So God firmly established the kingdom under him. The people brought gifts, and he gained great wealth and honor.

f.g: Gifts or tribute offered to the king.

n: His heart was “lifted up” — not in pride, but in courage and devotion to the ways of the Lord. He removed high places and Asherah poles.

f.g: Here a good sense: he was encouraged and emboldened in God’s ways.

n: In his third year Jehoshaphat sent officials to teach throughout Judah’s towns. Real reform requires teaching, not just tearing down idols.

f.w: to teach in the cities of Judah

n: Levites and priests went with the officials. Teaching was a shared effort of civic and religious leaders.
They carried the book of the law and taught people in every town. Scripture-based teaching is the foundation of lasting faith.

f.w: the book of the law of the LORD

n: The fear of the Lord fell on surrounding kingdoms so that none attacked Judah. Teaching God’s law brought national peace.

f.w: the fear of the LORD fell upon all the kingdoms

n: Even the Philistines brought gifts and silver, and Arabians brought 7,700 rams and 7,700 goats.
Jehoshaphat became very powerful and built fortresses and storage cities across Judah.
He had extensive supplies in Judah’s towns and experienced soldiers in Jerusalem.
His army was organized by family clans. Adnah commanded the largest Judahite division.
Next was Jehohanan, with another large division.
Amasiah son of Zichri is singled out as one who willingly offered himself to the Lord — a volunteer for God’s service.

f.w: willingly offered himself unto the LORD

n: From Benjamin, Eliada led archers and shield-bearers.
Next to him Jehozabad commanded troops ready for battle.
These commanders served the king in Jerusalem, besides those stationed in the fortified cities. The large figures, like others in Chronicles, may count military units rather than individuals.

f.g: Served under the king’s direct command.
